chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Madani from Musaddiq ibn Sadqa from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The woman in ihram may wear a ring made of gold." And when the woman is menstruating, there is no harm in her wearing a khilal (a type of ring or bracelet) beneath the garments. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَةُ: The female in the state of ritual consecration (Ihram)
key_terms.غِلاَلَةً: A type of ring or bracelet worn on the hand or arm

ai.seo_question: What jewelry can a woman wear while in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific exceptions for women in ihram, permitting the wearing of a gold ring and a 'khilal' (a ring-like ornament worn between fingers or toes) beneath garments, distinguishing these from the general prohibition of covering the face and hands. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh where certain adornments allowed for men are restricted for women during pilgrimage, yet specific items like the khilal are permitted under the condition of being concealed. The hadith underscores the practical flexibility in ritual consecration, ensuring that women can maintain modesty and comfort without violating the core tenets of ihram.
